questions.question: In Java, what is the contract between 'hashCode()' and 'equals()' that ALL well-behaved classes must satisfy?
options: If a.equals(b) is true then a.hashCode() == b.hashCode() must also be true
If a.hashCode() == b.hashCode() then a.equals(b) must be true
hashCode() and equals() must always return the same result for the same object
Two unequal objects must always have different hash codes
questions.answer: If a.equals(b) is true then a.hashCode() == b.hashCode() must also be true

questions.question: What is the effect of declaring a class 'final' in Java?
options: The class cannot be subclassed and all its methods are implicitly final
The class cannot be instantiated and can only be extended
The class fields become constants that cannot be changed
The class is loaded by the bootstrap classloader only
questions.answer: The class cannot be subclassed and all its methods are implicitly final

questions.question: Which of the following correctly describes how Java handles checked exceptions in lambda expressions?
options: Checked exceptions cannot be thrown directly inside a lambda unless the functional interface declares them in its throws clause
Lambdas automatically wrap checked exceptions in RuntimeException
Lambdas can throw any checked exception because they are anonymous classes
The compiler ignores checked exceptions thrown inside lambda bodies
questions.answer: Checked exceptions cannot be thrown directly inside a lambda unless the functional interface declares them in its throws clause

questions.question: What is the difference between 'Comparable' and 'Comparator' interfaces in Java?
options: Comparable defines natural ordering inside the class via compareTo(); Comparator defines external custom ordering via compare()
Comparable is used for sorting collections; Comparator is used for sorting arrays only
Comparator must be implemented by the object being compared; Comparable is always external
Both are identical — Comparator was added in Java 8 as a replacement for Comparable
questions.answer: Comparable defines natural ordering inside the class via compareTo(); Comparator defines external custom ordering via compare()

questions.question: Which statement about Java's 'try-with-resources' is TRUE?
options: Resources declared in the try header are closed automatically in reverse declaration order, even if an exception occurs
Resources are closed only if no exception is thrown in the try block
Only one resource can be declared in a single try-with-resources statement
The AutoCloseable.close() method is called before the try block begins
questions.answer: Resources declared in the try header are closed automatically in reverse declaration order, even if an exception occurs

questions.question: What does 'method hiding' mean in Java, and how does it differ from method overriding?
options: Static methods are hidden (resolved at compile time by reference type); instance methods are overridden (resolved at runtime by object type)
Method hiding occurs when a subclass declares a private method with the same name as a parent method
Method hiding and overriding are identical — both use dynamic dispatch
Method hiding applies to final methods; overriding applies to abstract methods only
questions.answer: Static methods are hidden (resolved at compile time by reference type); instance methods are overridden (resolved at runtime by object type)

questions.question: In Java multithreading, what is a 'race condition' and what is the standard remedy?
options: A race condition occurs when multiple threads access shared mutable state concurrently without synchronization; remedy is synchronization or atomic operations
A race condition occurs only when threads share the same object reference; remedy is to use separate instances per thread
Race conditions only occur in daemon threads; remedy is to use non-daemon threads
Race conditions are automatically handled by the JVM garbage collector
questions.answer: A race condition occurs when multiple threads access shared mutable state concurrently without synchronization; remedy is synchronization or atomic operations

questions.question: What is 'type erasure' in Java generics and what is its primary consequence?
options: Generic type parameters are removed at compile time and replaced with their bounds or Object; generic type info is unavailable at runtime
Generic types are erased when a class is serialized and must be re-specified on deserialization
Type erasure only affects wildcard types (? extends / ? super), not concrete type parameters
Type erasure converts all generic collections to arrays at compile time for performance
questions.answer: Generic type parameters are removed at compile time and replaced with their bounds or Object; generic type info is unavailable at runtime

questions.question: Which statement about Java's 'shallow copy' versus 'deep copy' is TRUE?
options: Shallow copy duplicates the object's primitive fields and copies references (not the referenced objects); deep copy recursively copies all referenced objects
Shallow copy creates a completely independent clone with all nested objects duplicated
Deep copy is performed automatically by Object.clone() without any overriding needed
Shallow copy is only possible for objects that implement the Serializable interface
questions.answer: Shallow copy duplicates the object's primitive fields and copies references (not the referenced objects); deep copy recursively copies all referenced objects

questions.question: What does the 'static' keyword mean when applied to a nested class in Java?

A static nested class can only contain static members
A static nested class is loaded at JVM startup regardless of usage
A static nested class cannot access any members of the outer class
